findings: The retained source states only a coding test for transfer under multithreading; the candidate therefore limits itself explicitly to a single-JVM in-memory account protocol instead of inventing database or distributed-transaction semantics.

Account representation, value type, insufficient-funds behavior, self-transfer behavior, overflow policy and lock primitive are not source facts; the candidate labels them as selected contract choices.
Both account locks cover the balance check, both new-balance computations and both assignments, so threads following this protocol cannot observe or create a successful half-transfer.

Acquiring unique account IDs in ascending order prevents the targeted A-to-B versus B-to-A opposite lock-order cycle; distinct accounts with duplicate IDs are rejected so the ordering key remains a strict identity.
Both new balances are computed before either assignment, so destination overflow fails before state mutation and does not leave a debit-only partial update.

The exact Java fixture was independently executed with OpenJDK 21.0.11 and produced 'PASS fixed=6 opposingThreads=8 opposingOps=160000 randomThreads=12 randomOps=60000 conservation=true nonnegative=true progress=true'.
No database ACID guarantee, cross-JVM safety, crash recovery, production incident, throughput metric or personal project experience is fabricated.
